pm_exper_user_4878_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: How do you cope when someone who’s been a big part of your life is suddenly gone?
pm_exper_user_4878_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) When I lost a mentor who had profoundly shaped my path in sustainable finance, I found it helpful to honor their influence by carrying forward the principles they championed — drafting policies with the same integrity they inspired in me. Sharing stories about them with colleagues and mentees kept their wisdom alive in my work. Over time, channeling the loss into meaningful action became my way of staying connected to their legacy.
(b) When I lost an elder family member who passed down our Chinese traditions, I found it comforting to prepare their favorite dishes during Lunar New Year, recalling the lessons they taught me about resilience and unity. Sharing those meals with relatives kept their presence woven into our celebrations. Over time, integrating their customs more intentionally into my life became my way of honoring them.
(c) When I lost a beloved hiking companion, I found it helpful to reconnect with the trails we used to explore, letting each familiar turn bring back memories of our adventures. Sharing those stories with friends who understood the bond kept their spirit present. Over time, planning new hikes in their honor became my way of holding onto the joy they brought into my life.
(d) When I lost someone important to me, I found it helpful to focus on the moments and values we shared, letting those memories guide me through the days that felt empty. Talking about them with people who cared helped keep their essence alive. Over time, finding ways to embody what they meant to me became a comforting connection to their memory.
